strings.app.name: FIFA Press App
strings.landing.title: Know what changed about your access, before you're refused
strings.landing.lede: A companion for journalists covering the 2026 World Cup. It shows what your accreditation currently permits, what has changed about it, and the reason attached to each change — so you find out from this screen rather than by being turned away at a barrier.
strings.landing.disclosureStrong: This is a portfolio demonstration, not a FIFA product.
strings.landing.disclosureBody: It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to FIFA. Every record, holder and decision in it is simulated. The match schedule is real; nothing else is.
strings.landing.signInHeading: Sign in with a demo account
strings.landing.signInBody: Two accounts are published on the sign-in page, in plain text, with the passwords. They open two different holders' records — and the difference between those records is the thing worth seeing.
strings.landing.browseBody: The match schedule and the help page need no account. Help is where the boundary of this service is stated plainly, including what it cannot do for you.
strings.landing.browseHelp: Read what this service does not do
strings.landing.point1Strong: Every change to your access, newest first
strings.landing.point1Body: — with what changed, why it changed, and what you can do about it. A change with no reason attached is not something this app will show you, because a change with no reason is what it exists to replace.
strings.landing.point2Strong: Warning before the consequence, where the consequence is foreseeable
strings.landing.point2Body: — a quarter-final allocation that depends on a fixture nobody has played yet is stated as a condition, naming both outcomes, rather than as a decision already taken.
strings.landing.point3Strong: How old the information is, always
strings.landing.point3Body: — not only when it is stale. A confident headline over hours-old data is the quiet failure this app is built to prevent.
strings.landing.signedOutBody: The simulated session has ended. Signing in again, as either holder, starts a new one.
strings.signIn.title: Sign in
strings.signIn.noticeSimulatedBody: There is no account system behind it — no server, no verification, and nothing that could tell you apart from anyone else.
strings.signIn.noticeCredentialsBefore: The credentials below are fake, published on purpose, and
strings.signIn.noticeCredentialsAfter: . They are the only two that do.
strings.signIn.noticeSessionBefore: The session lives in memory for as long as this tab does.
strings.signIn.noticeSessionStrong: Refreshing the page signs you out
strings.signIn.noticeSessionAfter: , because storing it would make this look more like an account system than it is.
strings.signIn.noticeBoundaryBefore: It is a demonstration of what this app shows a signed-in holder.
strings.signIn.noticeBoundaryStrong: It is not a security boundary and it protects nothing.
strings.signIn.accountsHint: Sign in as one, read the change list, then sign out and sign in as the other. The same conditional change sits on both records and behaves differently, and that difference is derived from the record — never from a setting either of them chose.
strings.signIn.failure: That identifier and password do not match a demo account. Both are published above.
strings.signIn.identifierRequired: Enter your email or credential number.
strings.signIn.identifierLength: This must be between 3 and 120 characters.
strings.signIn.identifierAllowed: Use letters, numbers, spaces, and the marks . - ' _ @ only.
strings.signIn.accountAmina: Has nobody at FIFA to ask, so a change that depends on an unplayed fixture interrupts her.
strings.signIn.accountTomas: Has a named contact who can answer a conditional question, so the same change is written to his record without interrupting him.
strings.record.title: My access
strings.record.signedOut: This record belongs to a holder, so it asks who you are first.
strings.record.signedOutLink: Sign in with one of the two published demo accounts
strings.record.signedOutAfter: — neither of them protects anything, and the sign-in page says so.
strings.record.errorHeading: No access state is available offline
strings.record.errorBody1: Your record could not be loaded and nothing is stored on this device yet, so this app cannot tell you what you currently hold.
strings.record.errorBody2: Do not rely on this screen at a barrier. Take your credential to the accreditation desk and ask them to read your current state from their own system.
strings.record.emptyBody: Nothing has been issued against this credential number. If you have applied, your application is still with the accreditation team and has not reached a decision — that stage has no updates to show, and this screen will fill in once it does.
strings.record.emptyLink: What this service does and does not cover
strings.record.noMatchAccess: No match access has been requested or granted yet.
strings.record.refreshFailed: The last attempt to refresh this failed. What you see above is the state stored on this device, at the time shown.
strings.record.noChangesAfter: Silence here means nothing has moved, not that nothing has been checked.
strings.record.name: Name

strings.detail.heading: Match {number} — {label}
strings.detail.unplayed: This match has not been played, so the teams in it are not shown.
strings.detail.signedOut: Your access to this match is part of your own record, so it is not shown until you say who you are.
strings.detail.signedOutLink: Sign in with a demo account
strings.detail.signedOutAfter: to see it, and to request access to this match.
strings.detail.accessError: Your access status for this match could not be read. This is not the same as having no access — it means this app cannot tell you either way right now.
strings.detail.barrierHelp: What to do at the barrier
strings.detail.dependencyHeading: An entitlement depends on this match
strings.detail.dependencyMocked: Simulated dependency. In this version the link between a fixture and an entitlement is mocked, and no results feed is connected.
strings.detail.gateIntro: Compare what this app holds against what the venue's access list says, as a barrier check would.
strings.detail.gateAgreeStrong: The venue list agrees with your record.
strings.detail.gateDisagreeStrong: The venue list and your record do not agree.
strings.detail.gateResolution: This app cannot establish which of the two is correct, and it does not try to. Show both timestamps to the accreditation supervisor at the venue and let them resolve it against their own system.
strings.detail.gateMocked: Simulated gate check. No venue access list is connected in this version, and which system owns that list is an open question this app does not answer.
strings.detail.statusRevoked: Access to this match has been withdrawn. See your record for the reason.
strings.detail.statusRequested: Requested. No decision has been taken yet.
strings.detail.statusNotRequested: You have not requested access to this match.
strings.request.heading: Request access to match {number}
strings.request.signedOut: Requesting access writes to a holder's own record, so this asks who you are first.
strings.request.signedOutLink: Sign in with a demo account
strings.request.signedOutAfter: — it is a demonstration, not a security check, and the sign-in page says so.
strings.request.mocked: Simulated request. Nothing is sent anywhere in this version — submitting writes a change to the simulated record and returns you to it.
strings.request.failed: That request could not be recorded. Your details are still here — try again.
